intro.speaker: aya
intro.text: This whole paper runs on two user-written functions. Let's see exactly what each one is supposed to do.

intro.speaker: aya
intro.text: Then we'll check the model against real examples, trace a job end to end, and design one ourselves.

L1U1.speaker: aya
L1U1.text: One function makes the intermediate pairs. The other one receives them, already grouped by key.

sourceRefs.quote: Map, written by the user, takes an input pair and pro- duces a set of intermediate key/value pairs.

L1U2.speaker: aya
L1U2.text: Same two functions, four different jobs - but reduce doesn't behave the same way every time.

sourceRefs.quote: Distributed Grep: The map function emits a line if it matches a supplied pattern.

L1U3.speaker: aya
L1U3.text: A job doesn't start with map workers running - something has to happen to the input first.

sourceRefs.quote: The MapReduce library in the user program first splits the input files into M pieces of typically 16 megabytes to 64 megabytes (MB) per piece

L1U4.speaker: aya
L1U4.text: Remember the shape every map and reduce function has to fit.

L1U4.speaker: aya
L1U4.text: Now design word-count yourself: one pair per word from map, one total per word from reduce.

outro.speaker: aya
outro.text: Map scatters, reduce gathers - and the same pair of functions reshapes itself for grep, counting, link graphs, and term vectors.

outro.speaker: aya
outro.text: And now you've seen the whole pipeline, from splitting files to the master waking your program up.

intro.speaker: aya
intro.text: Now the numbers: how fast these jobs really ran, and what they were used for at Google.

intro.speaker: aya
intro.text: Some of the timing claims sound right but aren't - watch for the difference between a milestone and the actual finish.

L3U1.speaker: aya
L3U1.text: A rate dropping to zero isn't the same as the job being done - there's still overhead and other work left.

sourceRefs.quote: The entire computation takes approximately 150 seconds from start to finish.

L3U2.speaker: aya
L3U2.text: Google ran MapReduce on all sorts of problems - some are general techniques, others are specific web or query analyses.

sourceRefs.quote: It has been used across a wide range of domains within Google, including:

L3U3.speaker: aya
L3U3.text: Picture one machine quietly getting slower and slower near the end of a job.

sourceRefs.quote: a machine with a bad disk may experience fre- quent correctable errors that slow its read performance from 30 MB/s to 1 MB/s.

outro.speaker: aya
outro.text: Backup tasks quietly save a lot of time - skip them and a sort job runs 44% longer.

outro.speaker: aya
outro.text: And MapReduce itself turned out to power everything from machine learning to Google Zeitgeist.
